propositions: Dense multi-criterion completion verification runs exhaust the full request budget on repository tools while banking zero criterion verdicts, triggering CompletionRecoveryError instead of returning evidence-backed PASS/FAIL verdicts.
Pydantic AI executes model response tool batches concurrently, so prompt-only instructions cannot enforce one repository execution per response or serialize evidence-before-record operations.

The completion contract requires incremental banking so partial progress survives bounded runs, but subjective prompt guidance (e.g., confidence-based record conditions) permits models to defer all bank writes until budget exhaustion.

An explicit finite-state wrapper at the tool execution seam atomically claims one governed action per run_step, counts three evidence responses per criterion, and invokes provisional met=false banking before returning on the third unbanked response.

The repair composes a new CompletionEvidencePolicy wrapper between memo and runaway guard layers, attaching only to privately flagged completion tools without changing public signatures, schemas, exit codes, or unflagged request behavior.

Held-out behavioral oracle validated RED (0/3 bounded success with policy disabled), GREEN (≥2/3 with policy enabled), and RED again under defect-seeded mutation, proving the finite-banking mechanism is both necessary and sufficient to replace zero-bank exhaustion with normal verdicts.
